Foundry, aligned with Kingdom — v4

Everything today's Foundry shows, given a visible home, and styled from Kingdom's tokens. The center is what you read while you talk; the right panel is reference about the thread, and the inspector takes it over when you inspect something. The table at the bottom lists where each item from today's viewer lands.

Companion: Foundry status catalog (every status, its symbol, the tokens).

Tab placement (a proposal: say “move X”)

Centre · the work's story

Thread (views /thread · /btw · /aside) · Plan · Loop
What you switch to and read: the conversation, the plan, how each turn ran (Loop includes the pointer ledger). These need the width. Under Plan and Loop the send box carries an About chip: comment on a step or a Loop row and the message is tagged “Re: …”; /feedback with a chip targets that item.

Right panel · what you glance at while talking

Work · Context · People · Permissions · Heralds · Feedback
Reference you keep in view beside the conversation; Work counts as glance (outputs, files, commits), and widens for diffs (⇤ wide, or open a file). The Inspector takes the panel over, with ← back to its tabs. Collapses to a strip ( ] ).

Top bar: Foundry and its pages on the left; on the right the Open and Incoming pills (each opens a dropdown), then Kingdom ↗ and the update status. The Workspace switcher (Threads · Board · Watchtower, keys T, B, H) sits in the top bar's centre, so only two chrome rows sit above the transcript. Both side panels collapse: the left list to an icon strip ([), the right panel to its tab strip (]), each remembered per view. Board and Watchtower show neither panel: the content takes the full width, and a card's Details opens a thread summary on the right; going back to Threads restores its panels. The nav footer is this machine and its resources: the device name and tunnel, every subscription with its 5-hour meter, the paired Kingdoms, and the Archives (local and hosted, with capture state). The thread header is the name on top, then pills: status, your agents (🤖) and people and parties (👤, grouped by actor), a Signet mark only when the thread involves Signets beyond its normal set; on the right project, Kingdom and branch (branch from 1440px), then the permission mode glyph, provider · model · effort, and context. What the thread is doing now is the top line of the waiting stack above the send box.

Every centre and right panel has a fixed header band (title, tags and key facts), the tabs at its lower edge, and a framed content area that scrolls below it.

What this version adds

  1. A thread header of pills: the name, then status, your agents, people and parties, the Signet mark when it applies, project, Kingdom, branch, permission mode, provider · model · effort and context. Model, effort, harness and mode are new: today's ThreadMeta doesn't store them.
  2. The stream carries today's per-turn detail, folded: the pre and post pipeline lines, “how this turn ran” (classification, route, exec), thinking word counts, the work log, a live status line with Stop, failure notices, message ⋯ revert / fork / feedback / inspect, prompt cards (approval, feedback tuning, Herald “this looks familiar”), held sends and member posts marked as data.
  3. Context gathers Linear, GitHub PRs and issues, Slack (threads, channels, DMs, groups: new), email, the repository, branch, worktree and session, the subscription and pool it runs on (from Kingdom), token use and the warm layers against the window.
  4. Participants use Kingdom's lens wording word for word, plus the floor, depth, conch, pause and invite. Permissions hold the access mode, granted approvals, and read-only Signet cards in Kingdom's style that link out to manage them. Signets appear nowhere else. Heralds are new: how the thread is shown to them, overlaps, related threads, past work and who is watching.
  5. Loop opens with the life of the work (plan → build → review → land), then the turn flow node by node (click a node to inspect it), the per-turn table, the learning loop and the pointer ledger.
  6. Statuses are solid shapes with a cut-out symbol, at most three symbols per colour. Archived is charcoal, clearly darker than idle.
  7. The board filters by project, by Foundry (your MacBook Pro, studio Mac), Forge Master and Global (maybe), and the counts follow the filter.
  8. Rows stay readable at 1200px: the name wraps to two lines instead of being cut; the project, status icon and counts sit on the second line. Subagents nest two levels deep at most; deeper ones fold under “+N subagents”.

From Kingdom vs owned by Foundry

Comes from Kingdom

  • Owners (personal, inixiative, Acme): the top-bar switch
  • Signets and permissions: read-only cards, managed in Kingdom
  • Integrations: links (GitHub, Linear, Slack, email, Archive)
  • Capacity: which subscription and pool a thread runs on
  • Foundry identity and pairing, devices
  • Visual tokens: one styling source for both apps

Owned by Foundry

  • Threads, their content and status
  • Participants, presence and the floor
  • The chorus, Heralds and the Loop
  • Feedback and its learning loop
  • Tasks, work, artifacts and diffs

Future ideas

  • Orgs attached to projects: the GitHub orgs and Kingdom orgs a project belongs to, shown on the project page (its Organisation section is the placeholder).

Open questions

  • Lime means three things: Kingdom's “yours / live”, Foundry's “working”, and primary buttons.
  • Row counts are neutral. Should the pending-prompt count alone be orange?
  • Work tab vs host apps. The viewer shouldn't grow runner features. Compare and file changes are shown read-only, “Open in GitHub” links out, and the worktree switch stays because today's viewer has it. “Merge main in” is gone.
  • Signet requests: from a known party they are an orange kind in Needs you. Incoming requests from outside parties with no Signet are not threads: they sit in their own Incoming band on the Board (and the top-bar indicator) until you accept them in Kingdom.
  • Two reds: the status red is deeper than Kingdom's error red so it never reads as orange.
